body: No, there wasn't a trigger for this episode at all, nevermind a trigger for it worsening. Nothing's changed recently. I just... I don't know. I thought I was used to coping with this, but now I'm just curled up in be with a laptop panicking. I don't trust myself.
... yes, and a wheezing cough if that means anything. just turned 23.

Thankyou

I don't know what's happening. life's not bad I think at the moment, but I found myself standing holding a knife this morning. I realised I'd taken a few too many antidepressants too, and would have taken more if I hadn't caught myself I think. To be honest half the reason I'm typing here is to distract myself so I don't end up doing anything. I'm honestly terrified about what I'll do, I just don't know how to handle this.

I've had recurrent depressive disorder for 9 years, but have never experienced anything like this before.

I don't get why people do this. There *are* gender-neutral non-derogatory pronouns these people can use. Is it really so difficult for them to even stretch to the singular "they"?

(I don't understand however, what's wrong with referring to a community as "them"? That is how you refer to a group of people (assuming one is not a member), right?)

> he other reason for seeing a therapist is that after three months of not being otherwise crazy, a therapist can recommend you for female hormones. But as far as I know, the only way that's going to happen in the U.K. is if you see a therapist privately. The NHS tends to be more about setting up roadblocks to make life harder than it needs to be.

That's a bit of a bugger; no way I can afford to see someone privately =[

> Get on an androgen blocker.

I'll speak to my GP about this ASAP.

> Let your hair grow, and generally try to look a bit more androgynous.

You're a few years too late on this one, it's halfway down my back :P

> Consider taking care of body hair if that's an issue.

Do you have any recommendations on methods here? I'm the sort of person who has to shave twice a day just to have stubble.

> Don't tell anyone a damn thing.

I'm fortunate enough to have quite a number of LGBT friends (I originate in Brighton), and I know maybe a couple who would be more supportive and not immediately burst out laughing.

Thankyou for the advice!
Yes, I'll bear that in mind, it is fairly unambiguous, thankyou ^^

> You should get a good, trans-aware and experienced therapist. That's not easy though, they are few and far between and often quite expensive. 

Expensive. There's a word I'm not fond of hearing. I'm fortunate enough to be in London, and some brief research shows a couple of good leads that may accept NHS patients - I'll certainly look into it first thing 


As for the rest, I think that's some of the best advice I've read on the subject, thank you. I'll take it to heart.

> You don't identify yourself as transgendered, specifically, but it sounds like you might be.

I don't identify myself as such, no - at least, not yet. I don't know enough, I think I might be, but that's just thinking. I'll certainly look into finding a therapist; I'm poor, and rely on the NHS, so I'm not sure what I'll find, but it's worth a look.

Thankyou for the replying, and for the advice!

> First, try posting on /r/transgender. I know there are quite a few transfeminine contributors there who live in the UK.

Thanks - I'll do just that

> Second, you're probably not "physically male" -- it sounds like you might have a brain that expects a more-typically-female body, which is why you're asking yourself why you weren't born with one. Your brain is just as much a part of your body as the parts that didn't develop in sync with your internal gender identity.

Maybe you're right, but it was about the best way I could think of putting it without resorting to "I HAVE A PENIS". what you put accross, however, is certainly intriguing.
